verdict: Nike's sales were flat at $11.3B and profit fell 35% to $520M — higher tariffs squeezed the margin, and a far higher tax rate than last year's one-off-flattered quarter did the rest.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: flat vs a year ago (-3% currency-neutral)

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — the one big region that grew, on wholesale demand.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Europe, the Middle East and Africa — up on reported numbers, down 7% without currency help.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: Asia-Pacific (outside Greater China) and Latin America.

segments.name: Greater China
segments.note: China — down again, -10% without currency help.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Converse sneaker brand — down across all territories.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Global brand divisions plus corporate leftovers.

opex.name: Demand creation
opex.note: Advertising and sports marketing — flat YoY, with higher sports marketing offset by lower brand marketing.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Salaries, technology and running the business — up 3%, including employee severance costs from the 'Win Now' reset.

takeaways.title: Sales went sideways
takeaways.text: Revenue was flat at $11.3B (-3% without currency help). Wholesale revenue rose 5% and North America grew 3%, but Nike Direct fell 4%, Greater China fell 7% and Converse dropped 35%.

takeaways.title: Tariffs squeezed the margin
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell 130 basis points to 40.2%, primarily on higher tariffs in North America. Inventories were $7.5B, down 1% — cleaner, but carrying higher tariff-driven product costs.

takeaways.title: The tax rate explains the profit drop
takeaways.text: Pre-tax profit fell 23%, but net income fell 35% to $520M: last year's 5.9% tax rate included a one-time, non-cash deferred tax benefit, while this year's rate was 20.0%. EPS was $0.35.

oneTimers: The year-ago quarter's unusually low 5.9% tax rate included a one-time, non-cash deferred tax benefit from U.S. tax regulations on foreign-currency gains and losses — the main reason net income fell 35% while pre-tax profit fell 23%.
Operating overhead included employee severance costs from the 'Win Now' actions (the amount was not broken out).
otherDetail: $15M of net interest income and $82M of other income.
footerNote: Segment revenues are Nike's divisional revenues; 'Global Brand & Corporate' combines Global Brand Divisions ($7M) and Corporate ($3M).
